title: fix(console): an approval request no longer links to a record whose object read the server refuses (objectui#11878)
body:
Fixes #11878

Clause-②: no

## What this does

An approver with no object-level read on an approval's target is still routed the request, but the server refuses every read of that object with `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. The Approvals Inbox readability probe used to swallow that refusal as "unknown" (the deliberate fail-open) and kept the record link, which landed on the record page's "Record not found — … may have been deleted".

Per ruling C on objectstack-ai/objectstack#7497 (Q5), a refused read now counts as "cannot read" **for the record link only**, exactly as an answer that leaves the id out of the row set (objectui#5211):

- `recordReadability.ts`: `probeRecordReadability` answers `'refused'` for every id of a group whose list read is refused. "Refused" is the `forbidden` kind of `classifyLoadError` (`@object-ui/react`), the read classifier `ListView`'s error panel, `RecordAttachmentsPanel` and the activity feed already share, so nothing here reads a status or code of its own. Every other rejection stays unknown (key absent), so the link stays.
- `useRecordReadability` now exposes two questions: `isUnreadable` (row-set answer OR refusal: the link's question, unchanged call sites on the row and in the drawer) and `isOutsideRowSet` (row-set answer only).
- `ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx`: one wiring change. objectui#8631's cause-free label (`unresolvableLabelFor`) reads `isOutsideRowSet`, so the ruling's "nothing else changes" holds for the label too.

The refusal is about the object, not the record: the server answers it the same for every id, existing or not, so withholding the link discloses nothing about whether the record exists. No access changes, no server change, no record-page change, nothing under `packages/`.

## Measured first (real browser, booted server)

Published `@objectstack/*` 17.7.0 (`objectstack dev --fresh`, installed in this run's scratchpad), a probe stack with one `private`-OWD object, a record-after-create flow whose `approval` node routes by a record field to a second user created by the admin, who holds no permission set on that object. Console from this branch under Vite, driven by Playwright/Chromium as that approver.

**Before (origin/main `9cb4e29`):**

- Inbox rows `INV-1002 Laptops` and `INV-1001 Office chairs` each rendered a link: `/apps/setup/probe_invoice/record/ID`. The drawer rendered the same link.
- The probe issued ONE list read for both ids (`top=2`, `select=id`, `filter` id in both) and got **403** `{"error":"You do not have permission to perform this action. …","code":"PERMISSION_DENIED","object":"probe_invoice"}`. Zero rows; there is no row set.
- Clicking the link: the record page made two by-id reads, both **403** `PERMISSION_DENIED`, and rendered "Record not found — The record you are looking for does not exist or may have been deleted."
- Control: the admin (who has read) issuing the same list read got **200** with both ids.

**After (this branch):** both rows render the title with no link; the drawer renders the title with no link; Approve and Reject are still there. Control in the browser: the submitter (admin, has read) in "Submitted by me" still gets both row links and the drawer link (probe 200, two rows).

## The PM's hypotheses, measured

- **H1, confirmed, with the shape measured.** Through the real `ObjectStackAdapter` (run live against the server above), the probe's read rejects with a plain `Error` carrying `httpStatus: 403` and `code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED'` (no `status` / `statusCode`): the client stamps both from the response and `find` rethrows it (it is neither a 404 nor an `enable`-block denial). The old bare `catch` dropped it as unknown, so `isUnreadable` stayed false.
- **H2, confirmed.** The row (`RecordCell` `href`) and the drawer branch already withheld the link whenever `isUnreadable` held, so the link needed no new wiring.
- **H3, measured and kept to the link.** The same probe feeds objectui#8631's cause-free label. Left alone, a refusal would also have switched title-less rows to "This record cannot be opened". The ruling moves the link only, so the label now reads the row-set answer alone. What the label shows for a 403: the record's title from the request snapshot (measured: the server snapshots `record_title` for this approver even without object read), and for a title-less row the reference text it showed before (the record id as `formatIdentity` prints it), now without the link.

## Pins (each against its ablation)

`apps/console/src/pages/system/recordReadability.refused-11878.test.ts`: the REAL `ObjectStackAdapter` over the real `@objectstack/client`, with only `fetch` stubbed in the server's own body shape:

- 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` → `'refused'` for every id of the group; one batched read.
- A refusal stays on its own object; a readable object beside it still answers per id (`true` / `false`, objectui#5211 unchanged).
- Fail-open controls, each leaving the key absent: 500, 503, transport `TypeError`, 401, `404 OBJECT_API_DISABLED`.

`apps/console/src/pages/system/ApprovalsInboxPage.recordLinkRefused-11878.test.tsx`: one page, one object per probe answer:

- refused (403) row: no link; title kept; no link in the drawer; still approvable;
- control (200 with the row): link with the same href;
- objectui#5211 (200 without the row): no link, unchanged;
- 5xx and transport error: link kept (fail-open, unchanged);
- title-less refused row: no link, the reference text it had, and NOT the cause-free label.

**Ablation**, from the committed fix, through `ablation-replace.mjs` (wrap mode, under the verify lock): anchor `if (classifyLoadError(err) === 'forbidden') {` → `if (false && classifyLoadError(err) === 'forbidden') {`, x1 → x0 on disk, blob `21cdf2ac1019` → `747d589254af`. Result `Tests 6 failed | 8 passed (14)`: all six refusal pins red (the two unit refusal cases, and on the page the row, the drawer, the title-less row, and the decide-after-withheld case), every control green. Predicted direction: red; observed: red. Restore: blob after restore == HEAD blob `21cdf2ac1019`, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Gates (local, on `c1ea60b` = this branch with origin/main `b6f8fc8` merged)

- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/console^...' build` (verify lock) → exit 0, scope 35 of 47 projects, 34 built, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check` → 0. `tsc --noEmit --listFilesOnly` lists both new test files and all 14 readability / inbox test files.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 apps/console/` (the console project, which includes every `recordReadability*` and `ApprovalsInboxPage*` file) → 0, `Test Files 164 passed (164)`, `Tests 1886 passed (1886)`. The lock printed `batch-last-exit` for that call because its parts were sequenced with `;`. Each part's exit was echoed and is quoted here.
- `check:control-bytes` 0 · `check:new-line-citations` 0 (`0 new citation(s)`) · `check:changeset-claims` 0 · `check:pending-changeset-literals` 0 · `check:vi-mock-specifiers` / `-inherit` / `-override-shape` 0 / 0 / 0 · `check:test-path-roots` 0 · `check:unreferenced-sources` 0 · `check:phantom-deps` 0 · `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` 0 · `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` 0.
- Lint, narrowed and measured: `eslint --format json` from `apps/console` (as its `eslint .` runs) over the 4 touched TS files: 4 files, 0 errors, 20 warnings. The two edited sources carry 1 and 19 warnings, the same counts their base versions give over stdin, so no new warnings. The root `eslint.config.js` sets no `project` / `projectService` (no type-aware linting), and no custom rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem, so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` belongs to CI.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:eager-closure`, reason: it reads the console's production build, which was not built. The new import (`classifyLoadError` from `@object-ui/react`) sits in the lazily loaded approvals page, and `@object-ui/react` is already a console dependency.

## Acceptance notes

- **The record page still says "Record not found … may have been deleted" for a 403 object-level refusal.** Measured above (two by-id reads, both `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`). That page is outside this card's fence (the claim excludes the record page's catch-all), and the card already names it as the dead link's destination. Reported for the seat; not changed here.
- **A title-less row whose read is refused shows the record id as plain text** rather than objectui#8631's "This record cannot be opened". That follows the ruling's "nothing else changes". Extending the label to the refused class would be one line (`unresolvableLabelFor` reading `isUnreadable` again) plus flipping the title-less pin. That is a maintainer decision, and it was not taken here. Not reproduced in the browser: the probe object has a title field, and the server snapshots it.
- **Read-only note, not reproduced:** `useRecordReadability` marks keys attempted before the probe answers and drops a cancelled run's answer, so a target-set change while a probe is in flight could leave those keys unknown (fail-open, link kept). A deep-link landing (`?request=ID`) on this stack was measured three times: one 403 probe and zero links each time.
